| D-025 | 2026-10-24 | security | round-locked-scans | A QR opens only for the round the team is in now. Scanning a QR from a later round (own path or not) returns LOCKED_MARK: the player is told plainly it is a later round's mark so they stop scanning it (never which round, never whether it is on their path); no clue, question, map, key box or scan ticket, and nothing is saved toward a later round. submit_key needs a scan ticket that scan_qr only issues for the team's current target, so a key typed for a later-round QR is refused (LOCKED_MARK) and alerted. Every locked scan or key try alerts the admin; 3 in one round raise a 'possible sweep' alert. No time penalty | User: a player who stumbles on a round-3 QR in round 1 must not get anything from it; teams must progress in order | — | ACTIVE |

A code from another team or before the final round is refused and alerted | User: the final QR must require a secret code; a printed key alone can be read by anyone who finds the final QR early | — | ACTIVE |

Each new function needs its own grant. | Supabase default privileges granted EXECUTE on every new public function to anon/authenticated; found by the Phase 2 integration tests on the test project | — | ACTIVE |
| D-029 | 2026-10-24 | product | multiple-choice | Questions mix formats (multiple choice, one word, number) and are dealt at random. Multiple choice always has exactly 4 options, shuffled per player. A wrong multiple-choice answer immediately replaces the question with another unseen one (no second try on the same question). Typed answers keep unlimited tries with the hidden 10/min limit. Multiple-choice questions never have hints, even when the admin enables hints. | User: with 4 options and free retries a player could tap every option; swapping the question on a wrong tap removes that, and a hint on a 4-option question is pointless | D-015 | ACTIVE |
